1.script: LIFE IN BHUTAN THE MYSTERIOUS HIMALAYAN KINGDOM WHERE HAPPINESS COMES FIRST Imagine living in a country hidden high in the Himalayas, where enormous mountains surround small villages, ancient monasteries sit above deep valleys, and forests cover much of the landscape. Imagine a place where television and the internet arrived only recently, where traditional clothing is still part of everyday life, and where a national policy once made the world ask a strange question. Can a country measure its success by happiness instead of money? This is Bhutan. A small Himalayan kingdom located between India and China.

2.script: From the outside, Bhutan can look almost like a forgotten world. There are no huge modern cities dominating the landscape. There are no skyscrapers stretching into the sky. Instead, there are mountain valleys, prayer flags, Buddhist temples, terraced fields, forests, rivers, and villages scattered across difficult terrain. But behind this peaceful image is a country facing a very modern challenge.

53.script: Weather can change quickly. And transportation can make it difficult to bring agricultural products to larger markets. Farmers have developed ways of working with the terrain. Terraced fields create usable farmland on slopes. Water from mountain streams supports agriculture. And families often combine farming with other forms of work. The relationship between people and land is especially important in Bhutan because environmental protection is part of the country's national identity.

59.script: WILDLIFE IN BHUTAN Bhutan's forests contain remarkable wildlife. The country is home to species adapted to very different environments. In the mountains, animals such as snow leopards live in remote high-altitude regions. In lower forests, other species thrive in warmer conditions. There are also Himalayan black bears, red pandas, takins, and many species of birds. One of Bhutan's most unusual animals is the takin.

65.script: A COUNTRY THAT CHANGED SLOWLY One of the most fascinating things about Bhutan is how recently some aspects of modern technology arrived. Television and the internet were introduced relatively late compared with much of the world. For generations, communities were much more isolated from global media. Today, that isolation is largely gone. A teenager in Bhutan can watch the same videos as someone in New York, London, Dubai, or Tokyo.
